Premiums, grace period and lapse
Each annual premium is due on the renewal date. A grace period runs until the end of the 31st day after the due date. (a) Each annual premium is due on the renewal date. A grace period runs until the end of the 31st day after the due date.
(b) If the premium is received within the grace period, cover continues without interruption.
(c) If a loss occurs during the grace period and the premium has not been received by the end of the grace period, the claim is paid less the overdue premium.
(d) If the premium is not received by the end of the grace period, the policy lapses with effect from the due date.

# DPO Handbook - Notification Deadlines

## Processor duties
Processors must tell the controller about a breach without undue delay; our contracts require this within 3 hours. This does not change the controller's own deadline.

## Applicable rules
- The controller must notify the supervisory authority no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach (a notification at exactly 72:00 hours is still on time).
- The controller 'becomes aware' when the security lead confirms that personal data was affected - not when the first automated alert fires.
- Notification may be made in phases. An initial notification counts toward the deadline only if it states the categories of data and the approximate number of people affected; otherwise the deadline is judged by the first notification that does.
- For the compliance report, classify each notification as: Timely; Late (under 24 h); Late (24 h or more).
- Timestamps from different systems are recorded in local time with their UTC offset; compare them on a single time base.

## Service hours
The service desk is staffed Monday to Friday, 08:00-18:00 local time, excluding public holidays. Messages received outside these hours are handled the next business day.

## Record retention

§6 Naming conventions
Attachments should be named with the case number first, then the document type, then the date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

§7 Privacy reminder
Only use the minimum personal data needed for a decision. Do not copy identifiers into free-text fields that are shared with vendors.

§8 Template feedback
Suggestions for improving this template can be sent to the methods team; they are reviewed once a month.

§9 What the signals tell us
Among burnout-driven departures, 55 out of 100 involved employees paid below their band midpoint. 65 out of every 100 departures driven by career growth involved employees paid below their band midpoint. Among departures driven by compensation, 20 out of 100 involved employees paid below their band midpoint. Among departures due to relocation, 30 out of 100 involved employees paid below their band midpoint. No promotion in three years is three times as common among departures due to relocation as among other departures. The engagement-survey attrition score misses 12 out of every 100 burnout-driven departures, and it wrongly flagged 34 out of every 100 other departures. It is not unusual for burnout-driven departures to lack the signal "above-average overtime": 70% of them do not show it. Among departures driven by career growth, 17 out of 100 involved above-average overtime. All but 22% of departures driven by compensation involved above-average overtime. Among departures due to relocation, 13 out of 100 involved above-average overtime.

§10 Assumption
Assume the pieces of evidence are independent of each other once the main reason for leaving is known.

§11 Other items in the queue (not this case)
File HR-70100 (February 25, 2025) was closed as "Relocation" by Rosa Kim. The employee's overtime was above average. That file has no bearing on this one.

§15 Audit trail

Garden leave may be applied at the company's discretion.

§17 Training reminder
All reviewers must complete the annual data-handling module before the end of the quarter. Completion is tracked automatically.

§18 What the review found
  18.1 According to an anonymous peer comment, the employee was paid below the band midpoint.
  18.2 The exit interview did not touch on it.
  18.3 The employee had not been promoted in three years.
  18.4 The engagement-survey attrition score did not flag this departure.
  18.5 The employee's overtime was below average.

§19 Holiday cover

  20.1 A fact taken from an anonymous peer comment may be used only if it was confirmed in the exit interview.
  20.2 Everything else in this file is admissible.

The on-call engineer at Lumen Cloud opened INC-56200 because the login API returned elevated 5xx errors. The affected service is payments-api, owned by the payments team.

2. FINDINGS FOR THIS INCIDENT
According to a customer-submitted report, service recovered only after a rollback. An on-call engineer reproduced it. The reproduction was done in production. The change-correlation bot returned no alert for this incident. The auto-triage classifier labelled this incident "Network/DNS fault". The logs contain connection-pool exhaustion warnings.

3. GLOSSARY
'Base rate' means the share of comparable past cases in each category before looking at anything specific to this case. A 'signal' is an observable fact that is more common in some categories than in others.

4. FOR REFERENCE: AN UNRELATED CLOSED FILE
File INC-66077 (April 7, 2025) was closed as "Config change" by Grace Brennan. Errors were confined to a single region. That file has no bearing on this one.

5. SYSTEM MAINTENANCE
The case-management system will be offline for maintenance on Sunday between 01:00 and 04:00. Save drafts before then.

6. ESCALATION CONTACTS
Weekday questions go to the duty lead. After 18:00 and at weekends, use the on-call rota; the rota is published every Friday afternoon.

7. BASE RATES FOR INCIDENTS IN THE PAYMENTS SERVICE
  7.1 Figures for incidents in the payments service:
  7.2 Of the last 2,500 incidents reviewed, 625 were incidents caused by a bad deploy, 875 were database-saturation incidents, 500 were network or DNS incidents, and 500 were third-party outages.

8. SEVERITY DEFINITIONS
SEV1: full outage for many customers; SEV2: a major feature degraded; SEV3: minor impact. Severity can be raised but not lowered mid-incident.

9. PORTFOLIO-WIDE BASE RATES
  9.1 Across all incidents across Lumen Cloud, the mix is different.
  9.2 Share of past incidents by category: Bad deploy 21%, Database saturation 21%, Network/DNS fault 32%, and Third-party outage 26%.

10. CHANGE LOG
v3.2 fixed a typo in the appendix; v3.1 re-ordered two sections. Neither revision changed any figure used in this review.

11. EVIDENCE STRENGTH
Share of past incidents in each category that showed each signal:
Signal                                | Bad deploy | Database saturation | Network/DNS fault | Third-party outage
--------------------------------------+------------+---------------------+-------------------+-------------------
recovery without any rollback         | 77%        | 79%                 | 80%               | 76%
flagged by the change-correlation bot | 57%        | 56%                 | 56%               | 56%
The auto-triage classifier names the true root cause 27% of the time, and its errors are spread evenly over the remaining categories. Connection-pool exhaustion warnings is 1.2 times as common among third-party outages as among other incidents.

12. TEMPLATE FEEDBACK
Suggestions for improving this template can be sent to the methods team; they are reviewed once a month.

13. WHICH EVIDENCE COUNTS
  13.1 Information that comes only from customer-submitted reports is disregarded unless it was reproduced by an on-call engineer.
  13.2 However, even then it must be set aside if the reproduction was done on a staging environment rather than in production.
  13.3 No other evidence is restricted.

14. ASSUMPTION
The methods team has confirmed the signals are independent given the underlying category.

15. UNRELATED MEETING NOTE
The quarterly staffing review has moved to Thursday at 14:00. Please update the shared calendar and send apologies to the chair if you cannot attend.

16. FOR REFERENCE: AN UNRELATED CLOSED FILE
File INC-39236 (January 2, 2025) was closed as "Config change" by Tariq Ortiz. The logs contain connection-pool exhaustion warnings. That file has no bearing on this one.

17. HOLIDAY COVER
During the end-of-year closure, turnaround targets are paused and resume on the first working day of January.

18. NAMING CONVENTIONS
Attachments should be named with the case number first, then the document type, then the date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

19. ON-CALL
On-call rotations change every Monday at 10:00 local time.
instructions: Given the base rates and the evidence, which root cause is most probable for incident INC-56200?
